# `silk/platform/linux/mapping`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Anonymous memory mappings from the Linux kernel, for programs that run without libc.

## When to use
Use [`Mapping.allocate`](#Mapping.impl.allocate) in a raw Linux program, after startup reads the page size from the
`AT_PAGESZ` auxiliary vector entry. Other programs get memory from the `Allocator` effect.

## Details
This module exists only on Linux on x86_64 and aarch64, with the `libc` profile set to `none`.
Each [`Mapping`](#Mapping) owns its whole mapping. Dropping the mapping releases it with `munmap`. Errors
are Linux error numbers, such as 22 for `EINVAL`.

## Gotchas
A raw pointer from [`Mapping.pointer`](#Mapping.impl.pointer) does not keep the mapping alive. If the program traps,
the mapping is not always released.

Import as `Mapping` with `import silk.platform.linux.mapping { Mapping }`.

Public declarations: 1.

<a id="Mapping"></a>

## `Mapping`

```silk
pub struct Mapping
```

One anonymous mapping from the Linux kernel that starts as zeros, and an aligned range inside
it. It exists only on Linux on x86_64 and aarch64, with the `libc` profile set to `none`.

### Details

Drop is automatic and releases the mapping. Use [`Mapping.release`](#Mapping.impl.release) to get the error from
`munmap`. Errors are Linux error numbers, such as 22 for `EINVAL`.

### Gotchas

A raw pointer from [`Mapping.pointer`](#Mapping.impl.pointer) does not keep the mapping alive. If the program traps,
the mapping is not always released.

<a id="Mapping.impl.allocate"></a>

### Associated function `allocate`

```silk
pub fn allocate(length: usize, alignment: usize, pageSize: usize) -> Result<Mapping, usize>
```

Maps zeroed memory with at least `length` bytes that start at an address aligned to
`alignment`.

#### Details

`pageSize` must be the page size of the process, from `AT_PAGESZ`. The mapping is larger
than `length` when it needs space to align the start.

#### Errors

- `22` (`EINVAL`) if `length`, `alignment`, or `pageSize` is 0, if `alignment` or `pageSize`
  is not a power of two, or if the size computation overflows.
- The Linux error number from `mmap` if the kernel cannot make the mapping.

<a id="Mapping.impl.length"></a>

### Method `length`

```silk
pub fn length(self: &Mapping) -> usize
```

Returns the usable byte count that was requested. It does not include the alignment space.

<a id="Mapping.impl.pointer"></a>

### Method `pointer`

```silk
pub unsafe fn pointer(self: &mut Mapping) -> ?[*]mut u8
```

Returns a pointer to the start of the aligned usable range.

#### Gotchas

The pointer does not own the mapping and does not keep it alive. Keep the [`Mapping`](#Mapping) alive
and access at most [`Mapping.length`](#Mapping.impl.length) bytes. The bytes are zero at first.

<a id="Mapping.impl.release"></a>

### Associated function `release`

```silk
pub fn release(value: Mapping) -> usize
```

Releases the whole mapping now and returns the result of `munmap`.

#### Details

Returns 0 on success or the Linux error number. After `release`, drop does not try to
release the mapping again.
